subject: info-doc
title: (R)INFO.DOC. ------CULT.SOLD.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-9 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan) opening Braxton's France analysis: 'creative black music has long enjoyed the support of the French public on many different levels … most people in France have some level of awareness about creative black music — which is not to say that every given person must necessarily like every aspect.' (R)INFO-DOC (the reality of information documentation) is crossed with CULT-SOLD (culture solidification): the question is what information-documentation produces in its actual instantiation when crossed with culture-solidification — the (R) prefix marking that real documentation (French television, radio, concert schedules) is what makes the crossing productive. (P)CULT-SOLD (point-of-activation culture-solidification) hangs at the upper-center. PHY-U-P (physical universe particulars) and MT-INFO (multi-information) cluster on the upper-right. STF (source-transfer functionalism) anchors the right margin. P-FC (point-focus) feeds into the subject from below-left. PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) sits centrally between subject and partner. AF-DY (affinity dynamics) hangs on the left margin. (R)INT (reality of interior) sits below. TRS (transference) and GRAD (gradualism) form the lower-center cluster. Structural argument: information-documentation-as-real crossed with culture-solidification is mediated by progressional-continuance as central hub. The (p) prefix on CULT-SOLD is load-bearing — the French case shows that culture-solidification operates here at point-of-activation (the live music event triggers it) rather than as sustained background. The diagram exposes Braxton's structural diagnostic of why France produces a healthy creative-music infrastructure: real documentation (broadcasters, concert venues) actually obtains, the progressional-continuance hub holds, and the point-of-activation cultural absorption keeps happening event-by-event.
